title: Experimental data on the removal of phenol by electro-H2O2 in presence of UV with response surface methodology
author: Malakootian, Nasiri, et al.

steps.title: Prepare chemicals
steps.instruction: Obtain hydrogen peroxide, FeCl₃·6H₂O, CoCl₂·6H₂O, HNO₃ (0.1 M), NaOH (0.1 M), tert‑butanol, and chloroform (CHCl₃) from Merck (Germany) and prepare any required stock solutions.

steps.title: Assemble reactor and electrodes
steps.instruction: Set up a 1.0 L plexiglass vessel equipped with two 1 mm‑thick aluminum plate electrodes spaced 5 cm apart; connect the electrodes in bipolar mode to a DC power supply capable of delivering current densities from 1 to 30 mA cm⁻²; install a 30‑W UV‑C mercury lamp (Philips) in a quartz sheath at the reactor centre and fit an aluminum cover.

steps.title: Add supporting electrolyte
steps.instruction: Add sodium sulfate to the reactor to achieve a final concentration of 0.1 M (Na₂SO₄).

steps.title: Introduce hydrogen peroxide
steps.instruction: Add hydrogen peroxide to reach the desired concentration between 0.5 and 4 mM (e.g., 2 mM for optimum runs).

steps.title: Set stirring and temperature
steps.instruction: Place the reactor on a magnetic stirrer set to 400 rpm and maintain the solution at room temperature using a water‑bath temperature control system.

steps.title: Adjust pH
steps.instruction: Adjust the solution pH to the target value (3–11) using 0.1 M HNO₃ for acidification or 0.1 M NaOH for basification, and monitor with a calibrated pH meter.

steps.title: Program experimental matrix
steps.instruction: Generate a set of 50 experimental runs using Design‑Expert software (version 7) with a central composite design, varying pH (3–11), H₂O₂ dose (0.5–4 mM), and current density (1–30 mA cm⁻²).

steps.title: Run electro‑H₂O₂/UV treatment
steps.instruction: For each run, set the DC power supply to the prescribed current density, turn on the UV‑C lamp, and operate the system for the required reaction time (e.g., 25 min for the optimum condition).

steps.title: Sample and analyze phenol and COD
steps.instruction: Collect samples and determine phenol concentration using the 4‑aminoantipyrine method and COD using the dichromatic closed‑reflux method, following standard methods.

steps.title: Calculate removal efficiencies
steps.instruction: Compute the percentage removal of phenol and COD using R = [(input − output)/input] × 100, and repeat each analysis at least three times.

steps.title: Record and plot results
steps.instruction: Record all data, calculate average values and standard deviations, and plot graphs with error bars.
